title: Hallstatt's twin in China
hook: An Austrian lakeside village, copied almost house by house in Guangdong.
peek: Hallstatt is a tiny village on an Austrian lake, famous for its postcard looks. In 2012 a full-scale replica of its centre opened in Huizhou, in southern China, complete with a lake, a church tower and pastel houses.
lede: Hallstatt sits between a lake and a steep mountain in Austria's Salzkammergut, home to fewer than a thousand people. In 2012 a copy of its old centre opened in Huizhou, Guangdong, built as part of a housing development by the mining and metals company China Minmetals. It has its own lake, a market square and a copy of the church tower.

bullets.text: According to reports at the time, the designers had studied and photographed the real village in detail before the plan became public. Many people in Hallstatt only found out from the news, and some were upset.
Feelings softened over time. Hallstatt's mayor travelled to Huizhou for the opening of the replica, and some in the village came to see it as free publicity rather than theft.
The copy is a housing estate, but it also draws day visitors, and its lakeside and pastel houses became a popular backdrop for wedding photos.

The replica is often credited with boosting interest in the real Hallstatt among visitors from China. The tiny village has since struggled with crowds, and in 2023 it briefly put up a fence to block a favourite selfie spot.
